answer: Agents gain voting weight only after completing randomly assigned tasks whose answers pass hidden tests and peer audits. Each task requires a bond, returned only for valid work; identities alone earn nothing. Audits are tied to time-limited credentials, so splitting one agent into many accounts does not multiply credit. A juniper, saffron, or karst task label may identify the work, not its reviewer. Flooding the economy therefore costs the attacker many bonds and the effort to produce independently valid results.
